Orange County shopping center websites: the 2026 index

By Noah, founder of Endcap. Published September 26, 2026 · Updated October 10, 2026

In September 2026, Endcap checked the public web presence of 298 multi-tenant shopping centers in Orange County, California. 194 of them (65%) have a page of their own, and 78 (26%) have their own website. Only 97 (33%) publish all four things a prospective tenant looks for first: available suites with sizes, a site plan, a named leasing contact and a brochure.

Key findings

  • 104 centers (35%) have no page of their own on any owner, manager or broker site we could find. A retailer searching for one of them lands on a listing portal, a map listing or nothing at all.
  • 116 centers (39%) rely on a single page on an owner, manager or broker website rather than a site of their own.
  • 150 (50%) list an available suite with its square footage, 156 (52%) publish a site plan and 144 (48%) name a leasing contact with a direct phone or email.
  • 58 centers (19%) show a logo of their own on the web. Most appear under the owner's or broker's name only.
  • Only one of the 193 pages we could test reached a good mobile speed score (90 or above in Google PageSpeed Insights). The median page earned 5 of 10 points, which corresponds to a mobile performance score of about 50.
  • About 48% of the pages we found show availability, contacts or brochures only through a script such as a listing widget, which means the information may not be read by search engines or AI assistants that do not run scripts.
  • The median center scored 61 out of 100. Among centers with a page of their own, the median was 78.

What the top centers do

These 25 centers scored 87 or higher, the top tenth of the index. Most of them are not the county's biggest malls. Many are neighborhood and community centers whose owners or managers keep a clear, current leasing page.

What they have in common:

  • 92% have a website of their own, and the rest have a dedicated page on the owner's or manager's site.
  • 100% list available suites with square footage, and 100% show where those suites sit on a site plan.
  • 96% name the leasing contact with a direct phone number or email.
  • 100% keep a tenant directory, which serves shoppers and shows a prospective tenant who their neighbors would be.
  • 96% offer a leasing brochure that opens without a form.

None of this requires a large budget. The centers that score well are the ones where somebody keeps the availability, plan and contact current. Our guide to attracting tenants to a small shopping center covers what an owner controls, and the first 90 days after buying a center covers taking over a center's website and listings.

The 25 centers in the table above can show the Top 25, 2026 Orange County Shopping Center Website Index badge on their website, leasing materials or social pages. No center can apply for it or pay for it; it goes to the 25 highest scores, and it is dated 2026 because we review the centers again each year.

How we scored each center

Each center was scored out of 100 on ten criteria, using only what was publicly visible on its official web presence on the check date: the center's own website or its page on the owner's, property manager's or leasing broker's site. Listing portals such as LoopNet and Crexi, map listings and social media were not scored, because the index measures what the center's own team publishes.

Scoring criteria and the share of centers that earned any points for each
CriterionPointsWhat earns the pointsCenters earning points
Dedicated web presence20Its own website earns 20; a dedicated page on an owner, manager or broker site earns 12.65%
Available space with suite sizes15At least one available suite with square footage, or a dated "fully leased" statement.57%
Site plan10A site plan viewable on the page or in a linked document.52%
Named leasing contact15A named person with a direct phone or email earns 15; a general line earns 8; a form earns 3.67%
Tenant directory10The current tenants listed by name, on a list, map or directory page.57%
Leasing brochure5A brochure or flyer that opens without a login or form.50%
Center identity5The center shows its own logo or wordmark, not only the owner's.19%
Secure and working5The page loads over HTTPS with a valid certificate.65%
Mobile speed10Google PageSpeed Insights mobile performance score, median of three runs, scaled to 10 points.65%
Property facts5Total square footage or number of suites is stated.48%
  • Which centers: 306 named retail sites in Orange County from OpenStreetMap, with city and county confirmed by the U.S. Census Geocoder. Car dealers, single stores, office buildings, closed properties and duplicates were removed, leaving 298 scored centers. OpenStreetMap does not include every center in the county.
  • When: all checks were made in September 2026. A center's website can change the next day, so each score is a snapshot.
  • How pages were found: web searches for each center's name, address and any other name it is marketed under, plus the property lists of owners, managers and leasing brokerages. Every center with no page found was searched a second time, usually with 8 to 16 searches and the listing broker's own site, before it was scored as having none.
  • Mobile speed: the median of three runs of Google PageSpeed Insights on the center's main page. Lab scores vary between runs, and pages on a large owner's platform reflect that platform.
  • Websites used: the most common platforms among the pages we found were WordPress (102), Irvine Company (27), Buildout (20), Wix (15), Squarespace (12), Property Capsule (11), Placewise (10), Mall Maverick (7), Webflow (5).

Owners, property managers and leasing brokers can ask for a center's scorecard or send a correction to hello@endcap.design. We re-check the page and date the correction.
